citation: Shechtman, N., Roschelle, J., Feng, M., & Singleton, C. (2019). An efficacy study of a digital core curriculum for Grade 5 mathematics. AERA Open, 5(2), 1-20. https://doi.org/10.1177/2332858419850482
report_number: Math Curriculum Impact Study (MCIS); IES/NCEE Goal 3 efficacy grant (Reasoning Mind RM-CC5, West Virginia). AERA Open 5(2):1-20. ERIC Grantee Submission ED595114.
design: Cluster RCT; assignment level = School; 56 WV public schools randomized (29 treatment / 27 control), 46 schools completed the 2-year study and provided data (23 treatment / 23 control); 1,919 Grade 5 students with WVGSA scores (940 treatment / 979 control); 71 Grade 5 teachers; subject = mathematics; grade = 5 (registry band 3-6). Treatment = Reasoning Mind RM-CC5 adaptive/blended digital core curriculum with ~60 hours of required content-rich teacher PD over 2 years plus implementation-coordinator coaching ('TPD for curricula'). Control = business-as-usual existing math curriculum/resources. Measurement year = SY2015-2016 (Year 2, end of treatment).
problems: SOURCE: Legal Gold OA article (AERA Open, CC-BY-NC 4.0) was Cloudflare-blocked at journals.sagepub.com via curl; extracted instead from the identical full IES Grantee Submission deposited openly on ERIC (files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED595114.pdf), which is the same AERA Open 5(2):1-20 published version (verified by header/DOI/page numbers). A Digital Promise DSpace copy also exists. PRIMARY FULL-SAMPLE CONTRAST is unambiguous (Table 2, Whole sample row). STANDARDIZER: authors define ES as treatment coefficient divided by the pooled within-group SD of student scores (both groups); for the whole sample this pooled posttest SD ~= 79.27 points, and COEFF -5.0 / 79.27 = -0.063, matching the reported ES = -0.06. The Grade-4-proficiency-level rows (Levels 1-4) and Female/Male rows are NON-RANDOMIZED subgroups (RQ2/RQ3 differential effects), recorded with outcome_role=subgroup and is_full_sample=false; they should NOT be combined with the full-sample estimate. NOTE a likely typo in Table 2: the Male subgroup reports ES = -0.10 but COEFF = -2.4 with SDs ~82-86 implies d ~= -0.03 (Male's reported -0.10 duplicates the Female ES); the full-sample row, which is what the meta-analysis uses, is internally consistent. Only one achievement test (WVGSA, a standardized independent state assessment) at one timepoint (end of Year 2); no other waves or instruments. ICC reported per row in Table 2 (whole sample = 0.13); SEs come from a 2-level MLM controlling for Grade 4 WVGSA, so cluster_adjusted=true and pretest_adjusted=true. Main finding was null (no significant treatment effect on Grade 5 math achievement).

effect_sizes.arm_label: RM-CC5 digital core math curriculum + teacher PD (treatment) vs business-as-usual; whole sample, ITT
effect_sizes.test_name: West Virginia General Student Assessment (WVGSA) Grade 5 mathematics scale score (computer-adaptive test + performance tasks); state assessment provided by WVDOE
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (spring 2016, end of Year 2 / measurement year SY2015-2016)
effect_sizes.g_method: Pretest-adjusted (Grade 4 WVGSA covariate) treatment effect from 2-level HLM (students within schools), COEFF = -5.0 scale-score points. Standardized by the pooled within-group posttest SD of student scores (both groups): s_pooled = sqrt(((940-1)*78.5^2 + (979-1)*80.0^2)/(940+979-2)) = 79.27; d = -5.0/79.27 = -0.0631 (matches authors' reported ES = -0.06). Hedges J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1), df = n_t+n_c-2 = 1917, J = 0.99961; g = J*d = -0.06313. Variance from impact SE (preferred): SE(d) = 5.4/79.27 = 0.0681; g_se = J*0.0681 = 0.06811; g_var = g_se^2 = 0.004637.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.10, Table 2 (Whole sample: Control N=979 M=2483.1 SD=80.0; Treatment N=940 M=2478.0 SD=78.5; Treatment Effect Grade 5: ES=-0.06, COEFF=-5.0, SE=5.4, t=-0.94, p=.348; Level 1 var=5743.6, Level 2 var=853.7, ICC=0.13). Model described p.9.
effect_sizes.notes: PRIMARY confirmatory contrast (RQ1). Not statistically significant (p = .348); main finding was a null result. SE (5.4) and ICC (0.13) come from the 2-level MLM so clustering is already accounted for. Treatment 'TPD' component = ~60 hours of required content-rich teacher PD over 2 years plus implementation-coordinator coaching to deliver the RM-CC5 blended curriculum. Grade 4 WVGSA (pretest) was equivalent between groups at baseline; correlation Grade4-Grade5 = 0.79.
